main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large sloped snow roof (rows ~8-50) over a plank front wall with an arched double door and two lit windows (rows ~52-76)
top_band: Snow roof slope from row 8 to row 50, in light snow tones (#f6f9fd, #dce5f1, #bccade) with a lighter eave band at rows 47-50. A dark row and icicles at rows 51-52 mark the step down to the brown plank front wall.
evidence: The roof is a large, clearly visible sloped surface seen from above, with a thick lighter eave band at its front edge. It reads like the tiled roofs of the Beodeul house references. A dark eave and icicle row sits directly under the roof, and the vertical wood wall below has its own shading. The door and windows have snow sills, dark frames and iron bands, so they read as set into the wall. The roof and wall are both clearly drawn. There is no receding side face.

style.evidence: The snow has about five lightness steps (white, pale, light blue-grey, mid, deep blue-grey) with clump and drift marks and per-row shading. The wood wall has several brown tones with plank grain, and the windows and door add warm accents. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean navy beside snow and brown beside wood, not black. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Colours per tile (9) are close to the stone-house reference (11) but below the first reference (18). Total colours (42) are below both references (66 and 185), mostly because snow is a narrow ramp. The piece is slightly lower in density but still reads as crafted and not like a sticker.
